purpose: Apply the same source-grading discipline to promoter, planning, campaign and analytical claims so that the Observatory can be independently checked without treating advocacy or marketing as neutral evidence.

status_legend.primary-supported: Directly supported by a promoter, consultant, council or statutory source.
status_legend.authority-supported: Supported by Lewes District Council planning/policy material.
status_legend.secondary-corroborated-pending-primary-a: Reported consistently by secondary/independent sources, but the exact primary document bytes/page have not yet been archived into this project.
status_legend.campaign-claim-unverified: Claim made by the campaign; retained as a verification target, not presented as fact.
status_legend.issue-in-scope: The issue is demonstrably relevant to the EIA/planning evidence, but magnitude or outcome remains unresolved.

geometry_legend.published: Geometry directly shown in a source drawing or authoritative dataset.
geometry_legend.indicative: Feature is proposed/required in principle but exact geometry is unresolved.
geometry_legend.illustrative: Analytical geometry used only to communicate scale or scenario.

claims.claim: Eton College is the landowner at North Barnes Farm.

sources.title: ECE Planning - North Barnes Farm
sources.note: ECE identifies the client as Eton College and Welbeck Land and describes Welbeck Land working in collaboration with landowner Eton College.

claims.observatory_treatment: State neutrally in the public evidence summary.

claims.claim: Welbeck Land is a promoter/project delivery partner for North Barnes.
claims.observatory_treatment: State role separately from land ownership.

claims.claim: The current proposal is for up to 3,000 homes.
claims.observatory_treatment: Use as the current maximum, not a guaranteed final dwelling count.

claims.claim: Lewes District Council planning-policy material identifies North Barnes Farm as Site 11EC, land between Plumpton Green and South Chailey.

sources.title: LDC LAA 2025 Appendix 3.1 - Residential and Employment Site Assessments
Lewes Local Plan Interim Sustainability Appraisal, Dec 2025

claims.observatory_treatment: Use the site reference as authority context. The current displayed polygon remains an analytical envelope until exact source geometry is georeferenced.

claims.claim: Welbeck Land describes a 25-year phased placemaking approach.

sources.title: Welbeck Land - North Barnes Farm case study

claims.observatory_treatment: Treat 25 years as a placemaking/maturation horizon, not automatically as the construction programme.

claims.claim: A 2029-2039 construction window has been reported for the EIA/scoping programme.

sources.title: Independent audit supplied to the project, 12 Sep 2026
sources.note: Reports that the EIA Scoping Report anticipates construction from 2029 to 2039.

sources.title: Brighton Chronicle, 27 Apr 2026
sources.note: Reports building work starting in 2029 and completing by 2039.

claims.observatory_treatment: Show the apparent distinction between construction period and 25-year placemaking horizon. Do not label the 25-year visual control as an official construction schedule.

claims.claim: The Don't Urbanise the Downs maps page publishes three reference maps showing the campaign's view of the site/landholding and its relationship to the South Downs National Park.

sources.title: Don't Urbanise the Downs - The Land
sources.note: Contains Map of Site - Sarah Graphic.jpg, Eton_College_land_map2.jpg and land_map_fields.jpg.

claims.observatory_treatment: Use only as a cross-check/reference for georeferencing against authority/promoter mapping. Do not republish or treat the drawn boundary as authoritative without permission and corroboration.

claims.claim: The campaign has asserted millions of additional vehicle journeys per year, including a figure of about 3.5 million.

sources.title: Don't Urbanise the Downs - campaign material

claims.verification_needed: Reproduce or test against the submitted Transport Assessment/EIA travel-demand assumptions before any numeric figure is presented as fact.
claims.observatory_treatment: Do not use the numeric claim as an established impact yet.

claims.claim: The campaign has described construction as lasting up to around 30 years.

sources.title: Don't Urbanise the Downs - campaign material

claims.verification_needed: Compare with promoter phasing and the EIA/scoping programme; distinguish construction from longer placemaking/landscape maturation.
claims.observatory_treatment: Not used as the Observatory timeline.

claims.claim: Flood risk, drainage, water resources and wastewater capacity are material issues raised by campaign/stakeholders and fall within the technical evidence required for a scheme of this scale.

sources.title: Don't Urbanise the Downs - Backgrounder July 2026
LW/26/0191 - Regulation 15 EIA Scoping Opinion record
sources.note: Planning reference establishes the formal EIA scoping process; detailed technical conclusions remain to be verified from submitted documents.

claims.observatory_treatment: Show as an unresolved evidence topic, not as a proven harm or proven absence of harm.

claims.claim: Bevern Stream, ecology/biodiversity and landscape effects are material verification topics.

sources.title: Don't Urbanise the Downs - Backgrounder July 2026
Lewes District Council Site 11EC assessment material

claims.observatory_treatment: Keep watercourse and ecological context visible; do not quantify impact until the technical evidence is reproduced and checked.

claims.claim: The current public 3D buildings, streets and site envelope are a scale study rather than final proposal geometry.
claims.observatory_treatment: Keep visibly labelled and prevent use as a survey, planning boundary or final masterplan.
